title: One year after opening our EV depot, here's what the numbers say
description: Our electric vans now run on 8 cents a mile of energy, down from about 40 cents on gas. A year of real operating numbers from our solar-powered charging depot in Oakland.

blocks.x: /assets/img/blog/ev-depot-oakland.jpg
blocks.alt: City of Oakland officials and partners with a Family Laundry electric van at the new EV charging depot

blocks.x:
**TL;DR**
• Energy cost per delivery van: **8¢ per mile**, down from about 40¢ on gas.
• Adding solar cut our electricity bill **43%**.
• Savings: **about $9,700 per van per year** in energy alone.
• CO₂: **about 14 metric tons avoided per van per year**, roughly 70 tons across the fleet.
• Built in two steps: a 17-port charging depot in late 2025, rooftop solar in early 2026.

A year ago, we switched on our EV charging depot at our San Antonio facility in Oakland. It was the biggest investment Family Laundry had ever made: roughly $1 million for a 17-port charging depot, followed by rooftop solar to power it. The City of Oakland [marked the opening](https://www.oaklandca.gov/News-Releases/EWD/EV-Charging-System-Provides-Business-Savings-and-Community-Benefits) as a model for the hundreds of delivery fleets operating in the city.
At the time, we said going electric had to make financial sense or we wouldn't do it. One year in, we can finally put real operating numbers behind that claim.
They're better than we hoped.
From 40 cents a mile to 8
Each of our Ford E-Transit vans drives about 2,500 miles a month, or 30,000 miles a year, picking up and returning laundry across Oakland, San Francisco, and the East Bay.
With the chargers alone, electricity cost us about $350 per vehicle per month. Once solar came online, that dropped to about $200.
That's a **43% cut in electricity costs**, bringing our energy cost to **8 cents per mile**.
The bigger number, though, is the gap between electric and gas. Here's what it costs to power one delivery van for 30,000 miles a year at today's Oakland fuel prices:
*Gasoline: 15 mpg at $6.04/gallon. Diesel: 20 mpg at $8.67/gallon.*
**Each electric van saves us roughly $9,700 a year in energy alone** compared with a gasoline equivalent. Multiply that across a fleet that runs nearly every day, and it adds up fast.
And the CO₂?
A gasoline van covering 30,000 miles at 15 mpg burns about 2,000 gallons a year and puts **17.8 metric tons of CO₂** out the tailpipe.

Our vans have no tailpipe. The electricity they use isn't entirely carbon-free, even with solar, so we counted it conservatively: assuming every kilowatt-hour came from California's grid, **each electric van avoids about 14 metric tons of CO₂ a year**.
Across five vans, that's **roughly 70 metric tons avoided annually**. Because much of our charging actually comes from on-site solar, the real figure is better than that.
What we've learned

Electrifying a delivery fleet is more than swapping a gas van for an electric one. You need reliable charging, enough range to finish the day's routes, and a way to keep electricity costs down. Building the depot was a big lift, and we couldn't have done it without our partners and contractors.
The savings also sit on top of real upfront costs, so we won't claim every business will see these economics on day one.

But a year in, the case for electric delivery in cities like Oakland looks strong to us. Our vans run predictable routes, come home to the same depot every night, and cover enough miles for the savings to compound quickly. Solar makes the math better still, and the depot is already sized for the fleet of 15 vans we're planning to grow into.
We went electric because we wanted cleaner air and a sound business, and we weren't willing to trade one for the other. A year in, we got both.
That's the most encouraging lesson from year one: sustainability and a sound business don't have to pull in opposite directions. Here, they pull together.
What we built, in two steps

**Step one: the chargers.** In late 2025 we opened the depot itself: 17 charging ports (two DC fast chargers and 15 Level 2) with energy management software, designed around [Port Power](https://portpower.us/)'s modular "Depot in a Box" and installed by [Finish Line Electric](https://finishlineled.com/). We had been charging at another of our locations, which the fleet had outgrown; the new depot gave us room to grow.

**Step two: the solar.** In early 2026 we added rooftop solar, installed by [Citadel Roofing & Solar](https://citadelrs.com/). A large share of the electricity going into our vans now comes from our own roof instead of the grid.

None of this would have happened without our partners. Grants came from the [Los Angeles Cleantech Incubator (LACI)](https://laincubator.org/), [PG&E](https://www.pge.com/), and the [Bay Area Air District](https://www.baaqmd.gov/). [Port Power](https://portpower.us/) and [Pacific Community Ventures](https://www.pacificcommunityventures.org/) provided technical support and financing.
About the numbers
Electricity costs and mileage come from Family Laundry operating data for five delivery vehicles. Annual figures are calculated from current monthly costs, not audited full-year expenses.

Gasoline and diesel comparisons use [AAA Oakland metro fuel prices](https://gasprices.aaa.com/?state=CA) as of October 26, 2026, with illustrative fuel economy of 15 mpg for a gasoline Ford Transit and 20 mpg for a diesel van.

CO₂ figures use [EPA emissions factors](https://www.epa.gov/greenvehicles/greenhouse-gas-emissions-typical-passenger-vehicle) of 8.887 kg per gallon of gasoline and 10.18 kg per gallon of diesel. EV consumption is estimated at 0.60 kWh/mile including charging losses, at the EPA eGRID California average of about 0.194 kg CO₂/kWh. The 14-ton figure assumes all charging comes from the grid and takes no extra credit for on-site solar. Manufacturing, fuel production, and other lifecycle emissions are excluded.

title: Premium laundry delivery, at your doorstep.
description: Since launching our delivery service in 2019, we’ve been obsessed with one thing: doing household laundry - wash and fold, fluff and fold, etc - really,…

blocks.x: /assets/img/blog/31e1f9_a07414935e884abbb997fd5eaec92127.png
Since launching our delivery service in 2019, we’ve been obsessed with one thing: doing household laundry - wash and fold, fluff and fold, etc - really, really well.
It's been a bumpy ride but today we’re proud to be one of the best-rated laundry delivery services in the Bay Area.
Here’s what (we think) sets Family Laundry apart:

In-house work: Our dedicated team of 30+ W-2 professionals ensures your laundry receives the love and attention it deserves, at every step of the way. From our drivers to our launderers, we never outsource.
Individual treatment: Every Family Laundry customer gets their own dedicated machines. Your laundry is never mixed with someone else's (of course).
Free and Clear always: We use only high-quality hypoallergenic detergents to clean, and Ozone-water to sanitize your laundry. The result: fresh, sparklingly clean laundry with a neutral smell.
Drawer-ready: Each laundry item is sorted, folded, and bundled by family member, making it easy for you to unpack and put away.

Less junk: We use only natural, non-toxic cleaning products. We avoid unnecessary plastic. We don’t use softener sheets, toxic products, or chlorine bleach. We believe it’s better for our customers, it’s better for our employees, and it’s better for the planet (did you know our delivery vans are all electric?).
Thank you for trusting us with your laundry. Your feedback is always welcomed and appreciated.
Family Laundry.

title: We bought a laundromat. What happened next blew our minds :-)
description: In 2018 Laura and I bought a run-down laundromat in Oakland and renamed it Family Laundry. What we initially saw as a “passive” (ha!) investment for…

blocks.x: In 2018 Laura and I bought a run-down laundromat in Oakland and renamed it Family Laundry. What we initially saw as a “passive” (ha!) investment for the family quickly became our full-time jobs. With hard work, incredibly good luck, and an ungodly amount of debt, we turned this little jewel of a small business into one of the best-rated residential laundry delivery services in the East Bay (we’re now in San Francisco!).

In 2018 we had three employees. As of April 2022, we have 30 employees (most of whom walk to work), a fleet of delivery trucks, and two cleaning facilities in Oakland. We’ve come a long way from our laundromat days, and we’re just getting started.

We run Family Laundry the way we think all companies should be run: we put employees first, we actively engage with the community we operate in, and we do our part to reduce our impact on the environment.

We had to put the breaks on online ads & marketing spending this year. As a business with relatively high fixed costs (think facilities, vehicles, repairs & maintenance, full-time employees, debt payments) and no external investors, there came a point last year where we had trouble just keeping up with our bills, never-mind splurging on more Google Ads.

Thankfully we were able to iron out our working capital issues thanks to a long-term loan from the Small Business Administration (SBA). As of this writing, we have a solid amount of financial cushion to help us continue investing in our operations and accelerate growth in the coming months.

We’re tackling a massive market. The market for residential laundry delivery is still in its infancy, but we think it could become several times larger than the Dry Cleaning and Coin Laundry markets combined. We’re not McKinsey consultants or economists, but we know from personal experience that a service like ours (or theirs, or theirs, or theirs, or theirs, or theirs) can be habit-forming. It’s hard to go back to spending hours washing and folding your laundry once you’ve experienced a service like Family Laundry.

The pandemic accelerated the home delivery market as a whole (groceries, takeout, alcohol, laundry, you name it), and we think it’s only a matter of time before many, if not most, US households outsource at least some of their household laundry cleaning chores to professionals like Family Laundry on a regular basis.
Let’s put this into context. Today already:
40% of American households outsource lawn care and gardening.
10% hired house cleaners in 2021.
23% ordered their groceries online at least once a month (2021).

If 10% of US households (12 million) outsourced their laundry (at an average cost of  $300/month) to companies like ours, the market for laundry delivery in the US would be “worth” more than $40 billion annually. Compare this back-of-the-envelope estimate to the declining dry cleaning industry ($8 billion) or the coin laundry industry ($5 billion), and you’ll understand why we’re excited to be in this space.
/assets/img/blog/31e1f9_1e6891d7abb44440a54dc318cb674e89.png
IMPACT. Yes, we’re obsessed with perfectly done laundry, but what really gets us excited is using Family laundry as a vehicle for social and environmental change.

We create good service jobs. If we were to name our special sauce, it would be our employees. They are the reason our service is so highly-rated, and we do everything we can to provide them with competitive wages and stability.
Standard benefits:
Accumulated paid time off
Health insurance
Paid breaks, lunch
Professional development stipend
End of year bonus

We’re minimizing the environmental impact of laundry. There’s nothing like owning a laundry business to witness firsthand how wasteful and polluting household laundry is in the aggregate (and we don't even offer dry cleaning). There's: the chemicals that go in, the vast amounts of water going down the drain, the natural gas used for hot water and dryers, the lint…Add to that fuel used for pickup and deliveries and argh….It’s an environmentalist's nightmare.
Fortunately, this is our business, and we can do something about it:
Our washing machines are efficient and high-extraction

We use top-of-the-line, high extraction machines that use 50% less water than conventional machines (our water bill was cut in half when we replaced our older machines) and reduce residual moisture to a minimum. That, in turn, means less gas is required to dry laundry.
2. We don’t use more stuff than we need

We've eliminated bleach, fragrances, liquid softeners, and softener sheets from our facilities while maintaining a very high standard of cleaning. Our view is that less junk in our customers’ laundry = less junk in nature. We only use premium free & clear detergents from Puretergent, and Ozonated water. No phosphates, phthalates, and other nasty chemicals ending in 'ates'….It’s a win for everyone, including our customers.
3. We source our detergents locally
/assets/img/blog/31e1f9_448efda35ee94aca836187614fc5745c.png

We estimate that we’ve eliminated about 80% of our plastic waste - and significantly lowered our carbon footprint (no trucking detergent across the country) - by sourcing our detergents locally with Oakland-based Puretergent. Now, instead of throwing away hundreds of plastic jugs every month (most of which end up in landfills), we just refill them with Puretergent.
4. We recycle water
We go through a lot of water. Literally millions of gallons every year. Not only is it depressing seeing all that greywater go down the drain...it's super expensive!

We recently installed a commercial-grade water recycling plant at one of our facilities to see if we could reduce our water consumption even more. A few months in, the system has already reduced our overall water use by 20% (as of April 2022). Our aim is to keep another 1.5 million gallons of water, or more than 2 Olympic-sized pools, from going down the drain in 2022. Pretty cool.
/assets/img/blog/31e1f9_bee40c08593e49b8ae022c3728d3bac2.png
5. Our delivery fleet is going electric in 2022.

We are currently replacing our fleet of gas-powered delivery vehicles with 100% electric cargo vans. We have 4 Ford E-Transit vans coming our way in the next few weeks, and can’t wait to get off our gas-guzzling ways.
/assets/img/blog/31e1f9_7f370257a958461b843406a1d8322dcc.jpg
See you next year!
David Macquart-Moulin
Laura Guevara

title: We acquired Sudzee in San Francisco!
description: Today we’re thrilled to announce our acquisition of Sudzee, the San Francisco-based laundry delivery company and a true pioneer in our space. With this…

blocks.x: Today we’re thrilled to announce our acquisition of Sudzee, the San Francisco-based laundry delivery company and a true pioneer in our space. With this acquisition, we expect to double our footprint in SF and accelerate our overall growth in the Bay Area.

Sudzee was founded by Selena and Paul Wiley in 2011, years before VC-backed startups like Prim, Wash.io, or Rinse came to market. Early on Selena and Paul invented (and patented) a uniquely secure, steel mesh-reinforced laundry bag paired with a 4-digit lock, that could withstand being left unattended on SF doorsteps.
/assets/img/blog/31e1f9_751dafcee8a34724b0bf204a2a892e6c.jpeg
That invention helped them establish a loyal base of customers in SF, many of who still use the bag to this day.
We look forward to serving Sudzee customers for years to come (feel free to keep using your Sudzee bag), and we thank Selena and Paul for trusting us with their business. Onwards!
Laura & David

title: Meet Julia Fry, CEO of Puretergent
description: This month we’re thrilled to feature our partner Julia Fry, Founder and CEO of Puretergent (Oakland, CA). Family Laundry uses Puretergent to wash almost…

blocks.x: This month we’re thrilled to feature our partner Julia Fry, Founder and CEO of Puretergent (Oakland, CA). Family Laundry uses Puretergent to wash almost 100,000 lbs of laundry every month!
/assets/img/blog/31e1f9_65dcc9ae379f47428ee695e75af05dd3.jpg
What is Puretergent?

Puretergent manufactures herbal laundry, dish & hand soaps, and cleaning products that are certified 100% biodegradable and grey water safe in refillable packaging. We're woman-owned, invented all our formulas, blend them by hand at our warehouse, and practice circular distribution to all our customers.
When and why did you start this company?

I started Puretergent in 2010 because I wanted to feel clean fabric without chemical residue. I'm a textile junkie, love vintage fabrics, hand knits, crisp poplin, linens, chunky canvas and denim, and soft vintage T-shirts. I want to feel the actual hand of the fabric, with no chemical residue or fake scents. Puretergent uses pure herbs for cleaning, without synthetic perfumes or softeners, or harsh ingredients that wear fabrics down over time.
/assets/img/blog/31e1f9_fe50c3c38d614cc2bb1ae4c966cf485f.png
Where are your products sold?

Our products can be found in local refill stores like Re-Up in Oakland, Fillgood in Berkeley, Source Zero in San Jose, and Resourceful in Lafayette. Ace Hardware in Moraga carries our laundry soap, MudPuppy's in Richmond washes all their dog grooming laundry with Puretergent, and Blue Skies child care centers clean with our All Purpose Cleaner. You can also buy our products on our website.
What do you like to do in your free time?

In my free time I like to hike, garden, cook, and sew stuff for my family - there's always a list of things they want me to make them.  My husband is a chef, so our dish soap has to clean lots of dirty pots and pans!

title: Compramos una lavandería. Lo que pasó después nos sorprendió :-)
description: En 2018, Laura y yo decidimos comprar  una lavandería en Oakland. Las condiciones del local no eran óptimas y era evidente que necesitaba mejorar. La…

blocks.x: En 2018, Laura y yo decidimos comprar  una lavandería en Oakland. Las condiciones del local no eran óptimas y era evidente que necesitaba mejorar. La llamamos Family Laundry. Al principio, pensamos que solamente era una inversión pasiva, pero pronto se convirtió en nuestro trabajo de tiempo completo. Con mucho esfuerzo, suerte y una enorme cantidad de deudas, hemos convertido nuestra pequeña empresa familiar en uno de los servicios de lavado  de ropa más codiciado en el East Bay, el cual sirve actualmente también en San Francisco.

Al inicio empezamos con solo tres empleados. Pero en el mes de  publicación de este reporte, abril 2022, ya contamos con treinta empleados quienes principalmente viven en el vecindario. También contamos con varios camiones y dos lavanderías en Oakland. Hemos avanzado mucho en corto tiempo y aún consideramos que estamos al principio de esta aventura.

Administramos Family Laundry con los valores que toda empresa debe anhelar: priorizamos a nuestros empleados, contribuimos activamente en las comunidades donde operamos y nos enfocamos en reducir nuestro impacto en el medio ambiente.

En el 2021 no invertimos mucho en avisos en línea y marketing. Esto es debido a que nuestra empresa tiene muchos gastos fijos (dos lavanderías, camiones, reparaciones, mantenimiento, empleados de tiempo completo y pagos de deuda) además de que no tenemos inversionistas externos. Como resultado fue un reto pagar las cuentas y ello no nos permitió invertir mucho en marketing.

Afortunadamente recibimos un préstamo de largo tiempo a través de Small Business Administration (SBA). Actualmente, estamos en una buena situación financiera, lo cual nos permite  acelerar nuestro crecimiento e invertir en operaciones en los próximos meses.

Nos enfrentamos a un mercado grandísimo. El mercado de lavado y secado de ropa con entrega a domicilio (wash & fold, fluff & fold) aún está en una etapa inicial. Creemos que nuestro servicio se puede convertir en un mercado hasta más grande que el ya existente con Dry Cleaning y lavanderías de autoservicio combinado. No somos consultores de McKinsey ni economistas, pero sabemos por experiencia personal que servicios como el nuestro o como estos que aquí referimos este, o este, o este, o este, se convierten en una necesidad para el cliente. Después que un cliente tiene la experiencia de tener ropa limpia y doblada, entregada directamente a su domicilio, es difícil abandonar la conveniencia del servicio ofrecido.

La pandemia aceleró el crecimiento de todos los servicios a domicilio incluyendo compras de comida, alcohol, provisiones, laundry, etc. Estamos seguros que pronto muchos o la mayoría de los hogares usarán servicios externos como Family Laundry para lavar, secar y doblar  la mayoría de su ropa.
Para ponerlo en el contexto actual:
40% de los hogares en EE.UU usan servicios de jardinería y cuidado de césped
23% de los hogares usaron un servicio de entrega a domicilio de compras de comida y provisiones por lo menos una vez al mes en 2021
10% de los hogares usaron servicios de limpieza de casa en 2021

Teniendo en cuenta  estas tendencias, podemos pronosticar que si el 10% de los hogares en EE.UU (12 millones) contratan un servicio de lavado  de ropa  como Family Laundry, el mercado de limpieza de ropa directamente a domicilio se puede valorar en $40 billones anualmente. No olvidemos que las familias gastan aproximadamente  $300 mensualmente por hogar para recibir este servicio. Sin embargo, comparemos esto con el mercado de tintorería, el cual  ha disminuido en $8 billones.  El mercado de autoservicio de lavanderías también ha disminuido en $5 billones. Con estas cifras en mente podemos ver el potencial de nuestra empresa familiar y sentirnos emocionados por nuestra participación y contribución en el crecimiento de esta empresa.
/assets/img/blog/31e1f9_1e6891d7abb44440a54dc318cb674e89.png

NUESTRO IMPACTO. ¡Estamos obsesionados con la impecable limpieza de ropa! Sin embargo, lo que nos emociona es usar Family Laundry como un vehículo para el impacto social y las  iniciativas para disminuir la contaminación del  medio ambiente.

Creamos buenos trabajos. El ingrediente mágico de Family Laundry es nuestro personal. Ellos son la razón por la cual tenemos el servicio más codiciado en el East Bay y hacemos todo lo posible para brindarles salarios competitivos y estabilidad laboral.
Beneficios:
Acumulación de tiempo libre
Seguro médico
Descansos pagados
Becas para desarrollo profesional o personal
Primas (bonus)  de fin de año

Estamos disminuyendo la contaminación del medio ambiente. La empresa nos abrió los ojos a ver como la lavada de ropa contribuye significativamente a la contaminación del medio ambiente. Los contaminantes incluyen los químicos que van en los detergentes, el gas que se usa para calentar la agua y correr las secadoras, la pelusa y la gasolina que usan los vehículos.
Afortunadamente, nosotros somos los únicos propietarios de la empresa y podemos tomar acción:
Las lavadoras son eficientes y de mayor extracción

Tenemos lavadoras que escurren eficientemente y que usan 50% menos agua comparado a las máquinas convencionales. Ya que la ropa se escurre mejor, esto significa que se mantienen menos tiempo en las secadoras, reduciendo el uso de gas. Después de instalar las nuevas lavadoras notamos que las facturas de agua se redujeron a la mitad.
2. Somos conscientes de la cantidad de productos que hay en el mercado que causan contaminación y por eso, solo usamos lo que necesitamos

Eliminamos el uso de cloro, perfumes, suavizadores en toalla y líquido. Con estos cambios seguimos manteniendo una calidad alta de limpieza. Al reducir el uso de químicos innecesarios, entendimos que a la misma vez reducimos el impacto al medio ambiente y cuidamos del bienestar de nuestros clientes. Usamos solamente detergentes sin perfumes y biodegradables hecho por Puretergent, sin fosfatos, ni ​​ftalatos o otros químicos que puedan causar efectos negativos a la salud de nuestros empleados y clientes.
3. Los detergentes que usamos son hechos localmente
/assets/img/blog/31e1f9_448efda35ee94aca836187614fc5745c.png

Hemos eliminado aproximadamente un 80% de desechos plásticos y a la misma vez disminuido nuestra huella de carbono ya que el detergente no se transporta desde lejos. Nuestra asociación con Puretergent (en Oakland) ha sido clave y ahora en vez de tirar tanto recipiente de plástico, Puretergent viene a llenar los recipientes.
4. Reciclamos agua

Usamos mucha agua, millones de galones al año. Es muy caro usar esta cantidad de agua y a la misma vez, es decepcionante saber que toda el agua gris que producimos se desperdicie. Nos enfrentamos a este reto e instalamos un sistema de reciclaje de agua comercial en una de nuestras lavanderías. Después de algunos meses hemos visto una reducción de un 20% en el uso de agua (cifra de abril 2022). Nuestra meta es reciclar 1.5 millones galones de agua, aproximadamente el tamaño de dos piscinas olímpicas en 2022.
/assets/img/blog/31e1f9_bee40c08593e49b8ae022c3728d3bac2.png
5. Camiones eléctricos en 2022
Actualmente estamos reemplazando nuestros camiones que corren con gasolina a camiones 100% eléctricos. Estamos ansiosamente esperando la llegada de ¡cuatro Ford E-Transits!
/assets/img/blog/31e1f9_7f370257a958461b843406a1d8322dcc.jpg
See you next year!
David Macquart-Moulin
Laura Guevara
